title: Console cost breakdown mock payloads (Standard Cost Model v1) — working data + UI tables
content:
Context
- Purpose: provide realistic mock payloads + sample tables for Console cost breakdown views.
- Audience: Console backend + dashboard UI, plus QA for staged rollout.
- Source of truth target: Standard Cost Model API (internal) v1 (schema_version = "cost-model/v1").
- This is NOT billing/invoice totals; it’s “standardized cost primitives” for observability + optimization (see PM thread in Slack product/1768589014).

Assumptions / what we’re modeling (v1 scope)
- Costs are computed as attributable USD for a request or aggregate time window.
- Required split in v1: prefill vs decode. Cache hit info must be visible (KV cache + prefix cache).
- Overhead appears, but is explicitly labeled and may not match invoice (allocation windows differ). Overhead included in standard output as "overhead_allocated_usd" with a policy_id.
- Batching and queue time are shown as drivers/metadata; we do not try to fully explain scheduler decisions in Console.

Console UI surfaces we need to support
1) Request details: “Cost breakdown” panel for a single request_id / trace_id.
   - Total cost + prefill/decode + cache effects + overhead.
   - Show warnings if estimate is low-confidence or missing telemetry.
2) Route / model aggregate: table for a time window (e.g., last 1h) grouped by route, model, deployment.
3) Diff view (optional later): compare two time windows or two configs (Console might call what-if later, but not required for v1).

Field requirements (Console)
Hard requirements (v1)
- schema_version
- time range: window_start, window_end (aggregate) OR start_time (request)
- identity: org_id, project_id, environment (prod/staging), route_id (or route_name)
- deployment context: deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), region
- model context: model_id, model_variant_id (if any), model_family (optional but helpful), quantization_profile_id (nullable)
- token accounting: input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens
- stage split: prefill_input_tokens, decode_output_tokens (or equivalent; see mock payloads)
- cost totals: total_cost_usd
- cost breakdown: prefill_cost_usd, decode_cost_usd, overhead_allocated_usd
- caching: kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1) OR kv_cache_{hit,miss}_tokens (preferred), prefix_cache_hit_rate (optional)
- batching: effective_batch_size_avg, effective_batch_size_p95 (or a single batch_efficiency_ratio)
- data quality: completeness (0..1), warnings[]

Optional (nice-to-have in v1)
- queue_time_ms, compute_time_ms (prefill/decode separate)
- confidence interval / bounds for aggregates: total_cost_usd_ci_low/high
- hardware SKU (gpu_type), runtime_version
- attribution tags: customer_tier, billing_group_id
- “unattributed” bucket in aggregates (when telemetry is incomplete)

NOTE ON REQUIRED VS OPTIONAL FOR UI:
- UI should render even if optional fields missing.
- If cache/batch metrics are missing, show “—” and a tooltip: “Telemetry not available for this request/window.”

-----------------------------
Mock endpoint payloads
-----------------------------

A) Single request breakdown payload (for /internal/cost-model/v1/estimate or /breakdown?request_id=…)

Example: hosted, streaming chat completion with partial KV cache reuse

Console rendering notes (single request)
- Show total cost prominently.
- Breakout rows:
  - Prefill compute
  - Decode compute
  - Overhead (allocated)
- Metadata row(s) below breakdown:
  - Model / variant / quant
  - Region / deployment
  - Tokens in/out + cache hit rate
  - Batch efficiency
  - Data quality warnings

UI notes:
- Hide cache subpanel entirely if kv_cache_hit_rate is null AND hit/miss tokens null.
- Show warning pill “Partial telemetry” with hover details.

IMPORTANT: For Console mocks, the payload above uses nested objects/arrays. That’s fine as sample API output, but the Drive doc itself is plain text.

If we need a smaller/flat response for UI perf:
- Console can request fields=... or group_by limited.
- Rows count must be bounded (top N + "other").


-----------------------------
Sample UI tables (what we expect to render)
-----------------------------

1) Aggregate table (per route + model)

Time window: 2026-02-16 21:00–22:00 (us-east-1)

| Route                  | Model                | Deploy  | Requests | In tok (M) | Out tok (M) | KV hit (avg) | Batch eff (avg) | Prefill ($) | Decode ($) | Overhead ($) | Total ($) |
|------------------------|----------------------|---------|----------|------------|-------------|--------------|-----------------|------------|-----------|--------------|----------|
| chat_completions_v2    | open-llama-3-70b      | hosted  | 18,423   | 12.84      | 4.02        | 0.231        | 0.71            | 48.12      | 92.41     | 12.90        | 153.43   |
| rerank_v1              | rerank-2              | hosted  | 9,021    | 2.31       | 0.00        | —            | 0.83            | 6.18       | 0.00      | 1.04         | 7.22     |

UI behaviors
- Sort default: Total ($) desc.
- Tooltip on Overhead ($): “Allocated per overhead/v1 hourly pool. May not match invoice.”
- If KV hit avg is null => render em dash + “Not applicable / not emitted”.


2) Single request breakdown table

Request: req_01HRF6M5D7Q5C7M8X0EJ0Y1J8F

| Component              | Cost ($)  | Tokens       | Notes |
|------------------------|----------:|--------------|-------|
| Prefill compute        | 0.00321   | in=812       | includes cache misses only (hit tokens reduce compute) |
| Decode compute         | 0.00597   | out=256      | streaming flush overhead included in decode in v1 |
| Overhead (allocated)   | 0.00066   | —            | overhead/v1 hourly allocation |
| Total                  | 0.00984   | total=1068   | data_quality=0.98 |

Metadata callouts (chips under the table)
- Model: rw-open-llama-3-70b (variant …2026-02-01)
- Quant: q8_0
- Cache: KV hit 17.7% (144 hit / 812 prefill)
- Batch: eff avg 5.8, p95 10
- Region: us-east-1 (hosted)


-----------------------------
Notes on confusing areas / open questions
-----------------------------
1) “Input tokens” vs “prefill tokens”
- For chat/text gen, we equate input_tokens == prefill_input_tokens in v1.
- If we later support multi-turn cached prefixes, we may want to distinguish:
  - user_prompt_tokens
  - cached_prefix_tokens
  - billed_prefill_tokens (??? careful; Console should stick to standard taxonomy, not billing)

2) Cache metrics naming
- Prefer hit/miss token counts because hit_rate is lossy.
- Console only needs one of them. If both present, compute hit rate client-side for display.

3) Overhead allocation stability
- Expect support tickets when totals don’t match invoices. UI needs clear copy.
- Suggested copy (draft):
  - “Overhead is an internal allocation of shared infrastructure and operations cost. Invoices use billing system totals and may differ.”

4) Aggregates bounding
- The API must cap number of rows; UI should handle "Other" row.
- For mock data we didn’t include "other" row yet. Might be needed for routes with >100 models.

5) Confidence intervals
- Would be good for Optimize; for Console, optional. If provided, show subtle “±” next to total.


-----------------------------
QA checklist using these mocks
-----------------------------
- Request page renders when cache metrics missing.
- Aggregate table renders when kv_cache_hit_rate_avg is null.
- Overhead tooltip shows policy id.
- Warnings list shows as non-blocking banner.
- Feature flag fallback: if cost-model API fails, Console shows legacy costs with “(legacy)” badge (per ENG-4825 plan).

Change log
- 2026-02-10 (FS): added dedicated embeddings example + missing cache metrics edge case.
- 2026-02-17 (FS): added CI bounds fields to aggregate mock; tightened required/optional notes after review w/ Chloe + Nadia.
